plain_text:
Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) refers to a group of symptoms
that occur together and cause pain in the abdomen. They also
cause changes in your bowel movements. The type of IBS you
have depends on whether you have constipation, diarrhea, or both.
Other symptoms may include abdominal cramping, bloating, or
whitish mucus in your stool. You also may feel like you haven't
finished a bowel movement.

You also may feel like you haven't finished a bowel movement.

plain_text:
The condition can be different for everyone who has it.

People with IBS may experience symptoms on some days
and feel fine on others. While IBS affects the digestive tract,
it does not cause damage or disease.

plain_text:
IBS is considered a “functional gastrointestinal (GI) disorder.”
That means there's a problem with how your brain and your gut
work together. This can cause your gut to be more sensitive,
which can lead to more bloating or abdominal pain. It can also
change how the muscles in your bowel contract.

plain_text:
Increasing physical activity and getting enough sleep can
help IBS symptoms. Mental health and relaxation therapies may
help manage the condition as well. There are even medications
to help treat some symptoms such as stomach pain, diarrhea,
and constipation. It's important to talk to your health care
provider before beginning any treatment.

Health has helpful information on different IBS treatment
methods, including probiotics, acupuncture, peppermint oil,
and hypnotherapy.
